description:
Replaces the sender chosen for the invoice emails of the company, and optionally their
defaults. It does not affect other emails. The sender is a replacement, not a merge: a
property that is omitted or `null` goes back to its default, which is to inherit the default
email domain of the account and to use `facturas` as the `local_part`. The response is the
configuration as it is after the change, including the address in effect.

- **`sender.source`:** when omitted it is `EMAIL_DOMAIN` if `email_domain_id` is sent and
  `ACCOUNT_DEFAULT` otherwise. `email_domain_id` is accepted only with `EMAIL_DOMAIN`, and
  `local_part` is not accepted with `BEEL`: any other combination answers `422`
  `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- **`defaults`:** omitted, the stored defaults stay as they are. `null` removes them. An
  object replaces all of them, so a property left out of it is removed. Sending an object
  requires the email customization plan: without it the call answers `403`
  `FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE`, and the sender is not changed. The templates accept the variables
  listed by `GET /v1/email-template-variables`.
- **`email_domain_id`:** an email domain of the account that has already been registered. A
  domain that does not exist, belongs to another account or was removed answers `404`
  `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_FOUND`; one that is still being registered answers `409`
  `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_READY`. Choosing a domain that is not verified is allowed: until it is
  verified, invoice emails go out from the default email domain of the account if that one is
  verified, and from BeeL. otherwise.
- **`local_part`:** up to 64 characters: lowercase letters, digits and the symbols
  `!#$%&'*+/=?^_\`{|}~-`, with single dots between groups. Any other value answers `422`
  `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- **Removed email domains:** when the email domain a company chose is removed, the company
  goes back to `ACCOUNT_DEFAULT` and keeps its `local_part`.
- **Credentials:** it changes the address real invoices are sent from, so it requires a live
  API key and the `companies:write` scope. A test API key answers `403`
  `LIVE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retry does not repeat the
  operation.
- **Environment:** the configuration belongs to the company and is the same in test and live.

BeeL API endpoint: PUT /v1/companies/{company_id}/email-configuration (reference: https://docs.beel.es)

CompanyEmailSenderSource.description:
What the company chose as the sender of its invoice emails.

- ACCOUNT_DEFAULT: no choice; it inherits the default email domain of the account.
- EMAIL_DOMAIN: one of the email domains of the account, in `email_domain_id`.
- BEEL: the address of BeeL.

Email.description: Email address (minimum valid email is 5 chars, e.g. a@b.co)

anyOf.description: The defaults of the invoice emails. Omitted keeps them; `null` removes them.

email_domain_id.description: An email domain of the account. Accepted only with `source` `EMAIL_DOMAIN`.

local_part.description: Part of the address before the `@`. Not accepted with `source` `BEEL`.

company_id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the company the operation acts on: its identifier, not its NIF. It is the only source of context: the account that owns it is derived from it, and the `BeeL-Active-Company` header plays no part. A company you do not reach answers `403`, and so does a company that does not exist, so the existence of a company in another account is never disclosed.

name: beel_update_email_configuration
